description: Delta preset for a repository whose default branch is dev and whose main branch is the stable line. Extend it alone: default.json already applies through inheritConfig, and extending it again would apply its rules and custom managers twice. Renovate opens every update on dev as default.json decides. On main it opens only the updates it would merge unattended that change what users receive. They go in one Saturday group, except vulnerability fixes and ghcr.io/actions/actions-runner base-image updates, which open at once.

packageRules.description: On dev, follow our own libraries' pre-releases (v1.3.0-dev.7 on the Go proxy, the npm dev dist-tag), so dev builds against the newest dev build of each first-party dependency. A stable release is cut from a commit that pins stable versions again. Images are left out: Docker versioning reads -dev.N as a compatibility suffix, never as a newer version.

Hold, on dev, a first-party library's releases built on the github.com/cplieger/go module paths from each consumer still on the old library paths, so no build carries two paths of one library (an error from github.com/cplieger/go/httpclient does not match httpx's sentinels). The rule above makes dev follow first-party pre-releases even from a stable pin, so without this hold the first such release would reach these consumers within minutes. Each consumer leaves the list in the change that moves it to the new paths, which also takes the held versions; a library joins the list before its first release on the new paths. The npm halves of the base repo's hybrids (keyenc, sse) are listed too: they now publish from cplieger/go, where the old repositories have no matching tag, so a dev pin on them blocks the consumer's promotion. A module with no major suffix is listed by its own name too, because a `/**` pattern does not match the bare path. Remove the rule when the list is empty.

Lock file maintenance runs daily on dev, before 4am like Renovate's schedule:daily preset, so dev tests against the newest transitive versions. The schedule set here outlasts the lockFileMaintenance object's own weekly schedule, because Renovate re-applies packageRules after merging that object.

fclones' crate license tree is rewritten in the commit that moves the pin, on both branches: the arm64 build refuses a crate set that differs from licenses/crates/MANIFEST, and nothing but this commit may change that tree on main (the main intake accepts it only beside this pin's update). postUpgradeTasks is not merged across rules, so this rule replaces default.json's repin task for this one dependency and repeats its command first. Both commands must match the self-hosted Renovate's allowedCommands; a failing one records an artifactError, which holds the pull request for a human.
Majors stay on dev, including the anime-offline-database pin whose majors default.json merges unattended: the cplieger/ci intake check refuses a major on main, so it could never merge there.
Update types default.json never merges unattended (rollback, replacement, bump) stay on dev.
Go toolchain minors (1.27 to 1.28) stay on dev, where they wait for approval with their modernization work. Go patches reach main.
A tool-registry tag that moved without a version bump (the default.json retag alarm) stays on dev for review.
A git-cliff release asset that changed under the same version (the default.json asset-swap alarm) stays on dev for review.
A TypeScript nightly pin stays on dev, where default.json holds each weekly move for review.
Base-image minors (alpine 3.24 to 3.25) stay on dev, because a minor replaces the image's package set. Base-image patches and digests reach main.

On main, base images get their patches as their own update. Renovate otherwise offers only the newest non-major version, so once a minor exists the rule above disables it and the patch main should take is never offered. This rule has no matchUpdateTypes because Renovate decides the split before it knows the update type.

renovate/renovate minors reach main, in the weekly group. Renovate patches only its newest minor and keeps no patch line for older ones, so the base-image minor rule above would hold main on one Renovate release while rebuilds move the OS packages under it, and a package update that needs a newer Renovate then breaks main's image until the next promotion. Majors stay on dev.

With its minors on main, renovate/renovate takes only the newest release there: the patch split above would also offer a patch of the current minor, a second update of the same image in the weekly branch. This rule has no matchUpdateTypes for the reason the split rule gives.
The same for the Go toolchain, whose minors the Go rule above keeps on dev.

ghcr.io/actions/actions-runner minors reach main. GitHub publishes most runner releases as a new minor, such as 2.337.0 to 2.338.0. It stops sending jobs to a self-hosted runner that has not taken a release within 30 days, and a minor counts as a release. The base-image minor rule above would otherwise hold main's runner until the next promotion. The runner rule after the weekly group takes these updates out of the group. Majors stay on dev.
devDependencies stay on dev: they never ship, and dev's tests cover them.

Files under example and test folders stay on dev. default.json lets Renovate bump the compose files and Dockerfiles there, but they ship nothing, and the cplieger/ci intake check on main accepts only files that ship.
Workflow and composite-action pins stay on dev: they ship nothing and reach main with the next promotion. This rule covers the github-actions manager.
The same for the custom managers that read workflow and composite-action files, matched by those managers' file patterns.

The web-terminal client pair stays on dev. The two packages install only in matching pairs, and a pair update can include an engine major, which main never takes, so a member moving alone on main would break the npm lockfile.
kiro-cli updates stay on dev, where default.json holds each one for a hand merge after its release is read. main takes the update, with any code the release needed, in the next promotion.

deadset-spec updates stay on dev. Each deadset analyzer's conformance record names the contract version it implements, so a spec update needs regenerated records that a Renovate pull request cannot produce. main takes the spec, with its records, in the next promotion.

Renovate leaves deadset's first-party pins alone in the three deadset repositories, because the release rounds move them through the fleet gate. A merged pin bump would cut a dev tag that cplieger/ci carries into every repository's dead-code check without that gate. Other dependencies of these repositories, such as github.com/cplieger/go/filesafe, stay on Renovate.
No lock file maintenance on main: no published artifact resolves its dependencies from a lockfile, so a lockfile-only change would ship nothing.

Everything left on main goes into one group that opens on Saturday before 6am. Every other rule that sets a group comes before it, so this group replaces them on main. Only the ghcr.io/actions/actions-runner rule after it takes updates out of the group. updateNotScheduled false keeps an open group from taking new updates during the week unless a rebase or a dashboard tick asks for it. Automerge is left to each update's own rules, so a hold added to default.json later keeps the group waiting instead of merging the held update. Vulnerability fixes skip the group and the schedule. The fixed branchTopic keeps one branch, renovate/main-weekly-dependencies: a patch from a separateMinorPatch rule would otherwise go to a second branch named patch-weekly-dependencies.

On main, ghcr.io/actions/actions-runner updates skip the weekly group and its Saturday schedule, and no release-age wait applies to them. Each one opens as soon as it is released, and its merge releases main the same day. GitHub pauses jobs to older runners as soon as it publishes a critical security release of the runner. Waiting for Saturday could then stop every runner built from main's image for days. groupName null takes the update out of the group, because Renovate groups only by a non-null groupName. The rule must come after the group rule to win. separateMinorPatch false offers only the newest release, as the renovate/renovate rule above does. A patch of the current minor then never opens a second pull request beside a newer minor. This rule has no matchUpdateTypes for the reason the base-image patch split rule gives. It changes no hold above, so majors stay on dev, and automerge is left to each update's own rules.
